Your Providence project

Plan the work around the rooms you still need.

If your Providence project is in an occupied home or a multi-unit building, access is part of the flooring plan. Tell us about stairs, shared entrances, furniture, and the rooms that must remain accessible. Those details help us discuss the sequence before agreeing on the work.

For existing wood floors, include hallways and connecting rooms in the walkthrough. Refinishing only one area can leave a visible finish change at the doorway; a new installation needs a deliberate transition. We can discuss the tradeoffs before you choose a scope.

Before your walkthrough

  • Note the floor level, stairs, and access for materials.
  • Identify rooms and shared entrances that need to stay usable.
  • Show the connections between new flooring and existing wood.

Answers before you start

Providence flooring questions.

Have a question about your own rooms? Ask for a callback.

Can you discuss flooring for a Providence multi-unit property?

Yes. Tell us which unit or rooms need work, whether they are occupied, and how the crew would access them. We can assess the flooring project and discuss access and scheduling before providing a written scope.

Do I need to leave during floor refinishing?

It depends on which rooms are being refinished, the finish selected, ventilation, and access through the home. We discuss the work area and return-to-use instructions for the chosen finish. Do not assume every room can be walked on the same day.

Can new hardwood meet the original floors in my home?

We review board width, floor height, direction, species where identifiable, and the existing finish. A transition may be the best way to join the areas. An exact match to aged wood cannot be promised from a photo.

What should I send for a Providence flooring estimate?

Send the room count, rough dimensions, photos, floor level, and any access restrictions. Mention whether the project involves removal, installation, or refinishing. Measurements and site conditions are confirmed at the walkthrough.

Is the in-home estimate in Providence free?

Yes. We offer a free in-home estimate. After reviewing the space and your project, we provide a written, itemized scope so you can see what is included before work begins.

How do I request a callback?

Use the form on this page with your name, phone number, town, and project type. You can include a preferred call time. We will contact you about the project and confirm next steps; the requested time is a preference, not a booked appointment. You can also call (401) 602-0958.
